subtitle: Committed bilateral official development assistance (ODA) that targets climate change mitigation, adaptation, or both, as a share of the bilateral ODA covered by the OECD's climate tracking.

title: Foreign aid given
subtitle: Net official development assistance (ODA) from governments and multilateral organizations, grants from civil society organizations. This data is expressed in US dollars and adjusted for inflation.

title: Foreign aid given per capita
subtitle: Net official development assistance (ODA), divided by population. This data is expressed in US dollars and adjusted for inflation.

title: Foreign aid given to least-developed countries as a share of donor's national income
subtitle: Net official development assistance (ODA), divided by donor's gross national income.

title: Foreign aid received as a share of national income
subtitle: Net official development assistance (ODA) divided by gross national income.

title: Foreign aid received
subtitle: Net official development assistance (ODA) from governments and multilateral organizations. This data is expressed in US dollars and adjusted for inflation.

title: Foreign aid received per capita
subtitle: Net official development assistance (ODA), divided by population. This data is expressed in US dollars and adjusted for inflation.

title: Foreign-born population of the United States, by country of birth
Foreign direct investment, net inflows as share of GDP
subtitle: Net inflows of foreign direct investment from foreign investors to the reporting economy.

title: Foreign direct investment, net outflows as share of GDP
subtitle: Net outflows of foreign direct investment from the reporting economy to the rest of the world.

title: Foreign Policy Free from Interference of other States Score
subtitle: Expert estimates by V-Dem. International treaties, organizations, and confederations not considered if the state negotiated its entry and is free to exit. International market forces and transnational corporations not considered. Higher scores mean more freedom. A score of 0 is approximately the average across all countries and years.

title: Share of land covered by forest
subtitle: Forest area includes land with natural or planted groups of trees at least five meters tall, excluding those in agricultural systems.

title: Forest area
subtitle: Forest area is land under natural or planted stands of trees able to reach at least five meters in height in situ, whether productive or not, and excludes tree stands in agricultural production systems.

title: Annual change in forest area
subtitle: The annual net change in forested area as a percentage of total forest area. Negative values indicate a net loss of forest, and positive values indicate a net gain.

title: Forest transition phase
Forms of homelessness included in available statistics
subtitle: Categories of homelessness covered in the available data source, such as official government data, news reports, or information from non-governmental organizations.

title: Fossil-fuel subsidies
subtitle: Fossil-fuel pre-tax subsidies, measured in nominal US dollars. This data is not adjusted for inflation or differences in the cost of living between countries.

title: Explicit fossil fuel subsidies as a share of GDP
subtitle: Subsidies are pre-tax and for both the production and consumption of fossil fuels. Production subsidies reduce the cost of producing coal, oil or gas. Consumption subsidies cut fuel prices for the end user, such as by fixing the price at the petrol pump so that it is less than the market rate.

title: Fossil-fuel subsidies per capita
subtitle: Subsidies are pre-tax and for both the production and consumption of fossil fuels. Production subsidies reduce the cost of producing coal, oil or gas. Consumption subsidies cut fuel prices for the final consumer, for example by fixing the price at the gas pump so that it is cheaper than the market rate. The data is expressed in nominal US dollars, and is not adjusted for inflation or differences in the cost of living between countries.

title: Free and Fair Elections Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which election violence, government intimidation, fraud, large irregularities, and vote buying are absent. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most free and fair).

title: Freedom of Association Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which parties and civil society organizations can form and operate freely. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most free).

title: Freedom of Expression Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent of free speech and the freedom of the press. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most free).

title: Freedom Score
subtitle: Data by Freedom House. The score captures the extent of free and fair elections, political pluralism and participation, a functioning government, freedom of expression and association, the rule of law, and personal autonomy. Higher scores indicate more freedom.

title: Freshwater withdrawals as a share of internal resources
subtitle: Freshwater withdrawals refer to total water withdrawals from agriculture, industry and municipal/domestic uses. Withdrawals can exceed 100% of total renewable resources where extraction from non-renewable aquifers or desalination plants is considerable.

title: Fruit consumption per capita
subtitle: Average fruit consumption per person, measured in kilograms per year.

title: Life expectancy at birth, projections
subtitle: The period life expectancy is the age to which a newborn can expect to live, if age-specific mortality rates in the current year were to stay the same throughout their life. Future projections are based on the UN's medium scenario.

title: Gross domestic product (GDP)
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: Gross domestic product (GDP)
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: Annual growth of GDP per capita
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation.

title: GDP per capita
subtitle: GDP per capita is a country's gross domestic product divided by its population. This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: GDP per capita
subtitle: GDP per capita is a country’s gross domestic product divided by its population. This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: GDP per capita
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: GDP per capita
subtitle: GDP per capita is a country's gross domestic product divided by its population. This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: GDP per capita
subtitle: This data is expressed in US dollars. It is adjusted for inflation but does not account for differences in living costs between countries.

title: GDP per employed person
subtitle: Gross domestic product (GDP) divided by the total number of people employed in the economy. This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: GDP price levels relative to the US
subtitle: This indicator measures differences in general price levels relative to the United States. A value below 1 means that a given sum of US dollars purchases more goods and services than in the US.

title: Gross domestic product (GDP)
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: Gross domestic product (GDP)
subtitle: This data is expressed in US dollars. It is adjusted for inflation but does not account for differences in living costs between countries.

title: Gender-affirming care
subtitle: Interventions to help transgender and non-binary people align their bodies with their gender identity. This can include hormone replacement therapy, surgeries, or psychological support.

title: Gender Development Index
subtitle: The Gender Development Index (GDI) measures gender inequalities in the achievement of key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, a good education, and a decent standard of living. Values close to 1 indicate higher gender equality.

title: Gender Development Index groups
subtitle: The Gender Development Index (GDI) measures gender inequalities in the achievement of key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, a good education, and a decent standard of living. The groups below define the level of equality in these achievements as the absolute deviation of GDI from gender parity.

title: Gender wage gap
subtitle: Difference between average earnings of men and women, expressed as a percentage of average earnings of men. This data is unadjusted for worker characteristics.

title: Gender Inequality Index
subtitle: This index covers three dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment, and economic status. Scores are between 0-1 and higher values indicate higher inequalities.

title: Gender of the chief executive
subtitle: "Chief executive" is defined here as the head of state or the head of government, whoever has more power over the appointment and dismissal of cabinet ministers.

title: Gender of the head of government
subtitle: The head of government is the chief officer of the executive branch of their country.

title: Gender of the head of state
subtitle: The head of state is the chief public representative of their country.

title: Average years of schooling, adjusted gender parity index
subtitle: An adjusted gender parity index of 1 indicates equal average years of schooling between men and women. Values below 1 favor men, and above 1 favor women.

title: Unadjusted gender gap in median earnings
subtitle: The gender wage gap is unadjusted and is defined as the difference between median earnings of men and women relative to median earnings of men. Estimates refer to full-time employees and to self-employed workers.

title: Lifespan inequality: Gini coefficient in women
subtitle: The level of inequality in lifespans within a country, measured between 0 and 1. A higher Gini coefficient indicates greater inequality in ages of death.

title: Hidden Hunger Index in pre-school children
subtitle: Global Hidden Hunger Index scores in preschool (under-5) children (GHI-PD), which considers rates of stunting, anemia, and vitamin A deficiency. This is shown for the time period between 1999–2009.

title: Global Hunger Index
subtitle: The Global Hunger Index tries to capture the multidimensional nature of hunger by calculating an index score from four key hunger indicators. It is measured on a 100-point scale where 0 is the best score (no hunger) and 100 is the worst.

title: Precipitation anomalies
subtitle: The difference in a specific year's total precipitation — rain and snow — from the 1991–2020 average, measured in millimeters, excluding fog and dew. Negative numbers indicate drier-than-average years.

title: Share of people who have zinc deficiency
subtitle: The estimated share of the total population in each country with zinc intakes below physiological requirements, 1990–2005.

title: Government procurement spending as share of GDP
subtitle: Government procurement spending is the purchase of goods, services and works by the government. It includes intermediate consumption (e.g. accounting services), gross fixed capital formation (e.g. new roads) and social transfers in kind via market producers (purchases of goods and services supplied to households).

title: Government revenues as a share of GDP
Primary government spending as a share of original budget
subtitle: Expenditures between 85% and 115% of the original budget is considered consistent with good international practices.

title: Gross national income (GNI) per capita
subtitle: Gross national income (GNI) measures the total income earned by residents of a country, including income earned abroad. This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: Gross national income (GNI) per capita
subtitle: Gross national income (GNI) measures the total income earned by residents of a country, including income earned abroad. This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: Gross public sector debt as a share of gross domestic product
subtitle: Gross public sector debt includes debt securities, loans, special drawing rights and currency. It is given as a proportion of GDP.

title: Annual growth of GDP per employed person
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation.

title: Countries with more than 25 species at risk of losing more than 25% of their habitat by 2050
subtitle: The number of species at risk of losing greater than 25% of their habitat as a result of agricultural expansion under business-as-usual projections to 2050. This is shown for countries with more than 25 species at risk.

title: Self-reported life satisfaction
subtitle: Average of survey responses in the World Happiness Report. The survey question asks respondents their current position on a hypothetical ladder, where the best possible life for them is a 10, and the worst possible life is a 0.

title: Hazardous waste generated per capita
subtitle: Hazardous waste is waste with properties that make it hazardous or capable of having a harmful effect on human health or the environment. It ranges from industrial manufacturing process waste to domestic items such as batteries.

title: Health spending as a share of total government spending
subtitle: Domestic general government health expenditure expressed as a percentage of total expenditure of the general government.

title: Percentage of population covered by health insurance
subtitle: Estimate of health insurance coverage as a percentage of total population. Coverage includes affiliated members of health insurance or estimation of the population having free access to health care services provided by the State.

title: Coverage of essential health services
subtitle: Coverage of essential health services is measured as an index on a scale of 0 to 100 (where higher is better). This index is based on risk-standardized death rates – which give a measure of healthcare access and quality – and whether common interventions are carried out.

title: Acute hepatitis death rate
subtitle: Death rate from acute hepatitis, measured as the number of deaths per 100,000 individuals. This is measured across all ages and both sexes.

title: Share of one-year-olds vaccinated against Haemophilus influenzae type B
subtitle: Share of one-year-olds who received the third dose of the Haemophilus influenzae type B vaccination (Hib3).

title: Government spending as share of GDP
subtitle: Total government spending, shown as a share of gross domestic product (GDP). It includes interest paid on government debt.

title: Death rate from HIV/AIDS
subtitle: The number of deaths from HIV/AIDS per 100,000 people.

title: HIV expenditure on prevention and treatment
subtitle: Total expenditure on HIV/AIDS prevention and treatment, expressed in US dollars. This data is adjusted for inflation but does not account for differences in living costs between countries.

title: HIV/AIDS deaths averted by antiretroviral therapy
subtitle: Estimated annual number of deaths from HIV/AIDS and the estimated number of deaths averted by antiretroviral therapy (ART). Estimates are based on treatment access, treatment efficacy, surveillance data, and epidemiological modeling.

title: Homicide rate
subtitle: Annual number of deaths from homicide per 100,000 people.

title: Homicide rate
subtitle: Annual number of deaths from homicide per 100,000 people.

title: Homicide rate
subtitle: Annual number of homicides per 100,000 people.

title: Homicide rate
subtitle: Annual number of deaths from homicide per 100,000 people.

title: Homicide rate from firearms
subtitle: Homicide rate from firearms, measured as the number of deaths per 100,000 people.

title: Homicides
subtitle: Annual number of homicides.

title: Homicides
subtitle: Annual number of homicides.

title: Housing discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity
subtitle: Only legal status considered, not enforcement.

title: Human Development Index
subtitle: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary measure of key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, a good education, and a decent standard of living. Higher values indicate higher human development.

title: Human Development Index groups
subtitle: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary measure of key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, a good education, and a decent standard of living. The groups below define different levels of human development depending on the HDI values.

title: Which countries include human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines in their national vaccination programs?
subtitle: This shows which countries provide and recommend HPV vaccines through routine services. People may still be able to receive the vaccine if it's not in the routine schedule – it might be optional or available commercially.

title: Human Rights Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which people are free from government torture, political killings, and forced labor, have property rights, and enjoy the freedoms of movement, religion, expression, and association. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most rights).

title: Human trafficking victims
subtitle: Total number of human trafficking victims officially detected by national authorities.

title: Prevalence rate of hypertension in adults aged 30-79
subtitle: Estimated share of the population with hypertension, based on population representative surveys and statistical modeling. Hypertension is a risk factor for chronic complications, including cardiovascular disease, and premature death.

title: Share of one-year-olds vaccinated against hepatitis B
subtitle: Share of one-year-olds who have received the third and final dose of the hepatitis B vaccine (HepB3).

title: Implementation of integrated water resource management
subtitle: Integrated water resource management (IWRM) is a process which promotes the coordinated development and management of water, land and related resources in order to maximise economic and social welfare in an equitable manner without compromising the sustainability of vital ecosystems.

title: Monitoring of sustainable tourism
subtitle: Monitoring is expressed as the number of data tables implemented within the Tourism Satellite Account (TSA) and the System of Environmental and Economic Accounts (SEEA). These tables organize and track key economic and environmental aspects of tourism, such as expenditure, production, employment, and resource flows.

title: Progress towards the implementation of UNCLOS
subtitle: Progress in implementing the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea through legal, policy and institutional frameworks. Higher values indicate greater progress.

title: Import of environmentally sound technologies
subtitle: Environmentally sound technologies (ESTs) are technologies that have the potential for significantly improved environmental performance relative to other technologies. This indicator shows the value of imported ESTs in current US-$.

title: Imported deforestation
subtitle: Imported deforestation is the amount of deforestation in other countries that is driven by the production of food and forestry products that are imported. This is measured in hectares.

title: Imported or exported CO₂ emissions per capita
subtitle: This measures the net import-export balance in tonnes of CO₂ per capita. Positive values indicate net importers of CO₂. Negative values indicate net exporters of CO₂.

title: Share of children in employment
subtitle: Share of children ages 7-14 involved in economic activity for at least one hour in the reference week of the corresponding survey (irrespective of school attendance).

title: New infections of HIV per 1,000 people
subtitle: Incidence of HIV among the uninfected population aged 15-49, expressed per 1,000 people.

title: New cases of malaria per 1,000 people at risk
subtitle: Malaria is a life-threatening disease caused by parasites that are transmitted by certain types of mosquitoes.

title: Rate of new tuberculosis cases
subtitle: Estimated rate of new tuberculosis cases per 100,000 people. This includes both new and latent reactivated infections.

title: Income inequality: Atkinson index
subtitle: The Atkinson index measures inequality on a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate higher inequality. Depending on the country and year, the data relates to income (measured after taxes and benefits) or to consumption, per capita.

title: Income share of the richest 1% (before tax)
subtitle: The share of income received by the richest 1% of the population. Income here is measured before taxes and benefits. The dotted lines represent extrapolations due to limited data availability.

title: Average income of small-scale food producers
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries. In some countries small-scale food producers are running at a loss, this is reflected as a negative income.

title: Indian rhino population
subtitle: Estimated number of Greater One-Horned rhinos.

title: Industrial water as a share of total water withdrawals
subtitle: Industrial water withdrawals as a percentage of total water withdrawals (which is the sum of water used for agriculture, industry, and municipal purposes).

title: Industrial water withdrawal
subtitle: This measures the annual quantity of self-supplied water withdrawn for industrial uses, in cubic meters (m³) per year. It includes water for the cooling of thermoelectric and nuclear power plants, but it does not include hydropower. Water withdrawn by industries that are connected to the public supply network is generally included in municipal water withdrawal.

title: Industry jobs as a share of total employment
Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index
subtitle: The Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI) is a summary measure of key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, a good education, and a decent standard of living, adjusted for inequalities in these dimensions. Higher values indicate higher and more equal human development.

title: Inequality in education
subtitle: The Atkinson index measures inequality on a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate higher inequality. Inequality is measured here in terms of the number of years adults older than 25 participated in formal education.

title: Inequality in life expectancy
subtitle: The Atkinson index measures inequality on a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate higher inequality. Inequality is measured here in terms of the number of years a newborn would live if age-specific mortality rates in the current year were to stay the same throughout its life.

title: Infant mortality rate
subtitle: Estimated share of newborns who die before their first birthday. A rate of 1% means one death for every 100 live births.

title: Infectious and parasitic diseases death rate
subtitle: The reported annual death rate from infectious and parasitic diseases per 100,000 people, based on the underlying cause listed on death certificates.

title: Death rate from infectious diseases
subtitle: Estimated annual number of deaths from HIV/AIDS, diarrhea, malaria, respiratory infections, and all other infectious diseases per 100,000 people.

title: Death rate from infectious diseases
subtitle: Estimated annual number of deaths from HIV/AIDS, diarrhea, malaria, respiratory infections, and all other infectious diseases per 100,000 people.

title: Inflation of consumer prices
subtitle: Annual changes in the cost to the average consumer of acquiring a set basket of goods and services. This measure is used to track changes in living costs over time.

title: Flu vaccination coverage in the over-65's
subtitle: Share of people aged over 65 who received an annual influenza vaccine.

title: Share of workers in informal employment in the agricultural sector
subtitle: Share of employed people working in jobs that lack basic social or legal protection and employment benefits. Does not include illegal and illicit activities. The agricultural sector includes agriculture, forestry, and fishing.

title: Insecticide use
subtitle: Annual quantity of insecticides used in agriculture, measured as the tonnes of active ingredient per year.

title: Installed geothermal energy capacity
subtitle: Cumulative installed capacity of geothermal energy, measured in megawatts.

title: Installed solar energy capacity
subtitle: Cumulative installed solar capacity, measured in gigawatts (GW).

title: Intensity of multidimensional poverty
subtitle: Multidimensional poverty is defined as being deprived in a range of health, education and living standards indicators. The intensity is the share of indicators in which people in multidimensional poverty are deprived on average.

title: People displaced internally by natural disasters
subtitle: Internally-displaced persons are defined as people or groups of people who have been forced or obliged to flee or to leave their homes or places of habitual residence, as a result of natural or human-made disasters and who have not crossed an international border.

title: International finance received for clean energy
subtitle: International financing to developing countries in support of clean energy research and development and renewable energy production. This data is expressed in US dollars. It is adjusted for inflation but does not account for differences in living costs between countries.

title: International tourist departures per 1,000 people
Arrivals of tourists from abroad
Intersex infant surgeries banned
subtitle: Medical procedures on newborns or infants with physical sex characteristics that do differ from typical male or female bodies, usually without the informed consent of the child who is too young to participate in the decision-making process.

title: Number of people requiring treatment against neglected tropical diseases
subtitle: Estimated number of people requiring medical treatment for neglected tropical diseases (NTDs).

title: Is antibiotic use in livestock above proposed guidelines from antimicrobial resistance researchers?
subtitle: Antibiotic use is measured in milligrams per kilogram of livestock, adjusted to give a population-corrected unit (PCU). Researchers working on antimicrobial resistance have proposed a threshold of 50mg per PCU, which is shown as a threshold here.

title: Which countries are members of the International Whaling Commission?
subtitle: The International Whaling Commission (IWC) was set up to preserve global whale stocks through catch quotes, regulation of hunting methods and designation of specific hunting areas.

title: Javan rhino population
subtitle: Estimated number of Javan rhinos.

title: Joint adoptions by same-sex partners
subtitle: Same-sex partners can adopt a child legally, with both parents being recognized as such.

title: Judicial Checks on Government Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which the executive respects the constitution and complies with the rulings of independent courts. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most constrained).

title: Judicial Corruption Score
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of how often individuals or businesses make undocumented extra payments or bribes to obtain a favorable judicial decision, or speed up or delay the process. Higher scores mean less corruption. A score of 0 is approximately the average across all countries and years.

title: Labor force participation rate
subtitle: Share of the working-age population (ages 15 and over) who are economically active (employed or unemployed).

title: Productivity: output per hour worked
subtitle: Productivity is measured as gross domestic product (GDP) per hour of work. This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.

title: Labor share of gross domestic product (GDP)
subtitle: The labor share of gross domestic product (GDP) is the estimated total compensation of employees given as a percent of GDP. It provides information about the relative share of output paid as compensation to employees, compared to the share paid to capital.

title: Land area in hectares
subtitle:
Total land area, measured in hectares. 100 hectares is one square kilometer.
Land area is a country's total area, excluding area under inland water bodies, national claims to continental shelf, and exclusive economic zones. In most cases the definition of inland water bodies includes major rivers and lakes.

title: Land area in square kilometers
subtitle: Total land area, measured in square kilometers (km²). Land area is a country's total area, excluding area under inland water bodies, national claims to continental shelf, and exclusive economic zones. In most cases the definition of inland water bodies includes major rivers and lakes.

title: Land used for agriculture
subtitle: Agricultural land use is the sum of croplands and pasture – land used for grazing livestock. It is measured in hectares.

title: Land use for palm oil production
Landline Internet subscriptions
subtitle: Subscriptions to fixed access to the public Internet with a download speed of at least 256 kbit/s.

title: Share of population with very large health spending
subtitle: The share of the population that spend more than 25% of total household expenditure or income on health.

title: Employment discrimination based on gender prohibited
subtitle: The law prohibits employers from discriminating based on sex or gender, or mandates equal treatment of women and men in employment.

title: Mean lead concentrations in the blood of children
subtitle: Mean lead concentrations in the blood of children aged 0 to 14 years old between 2010 and 2019. There is no defined 'safe' level for lead blood concentrations. The WHO adopts a threshold of 5 µg/dL as an achievable maximum level in children.

title: Share of paints with lead levels greater than 10,000 ppm
subtitle: Lead paint is a significant contributor to lead poisoning; many countries have therefore implemented a regulatory limit of 90 parts per million (ppm) or 600ppm per weight of dry paint. Values here show the share of lead paint samples with more than 10,000ppm per weight of dry paint.

title: Share of paints with lead levels greater than 600 ppm
subtitle: Lead paint is thought to be a significant contributor to lead poisoning; many countries have therefore implemented a regulatory limit of 90 parts per million (ppm) or 600ppm per weight of dry paint.

title: Share of paints with lead levels greater than 90 ppm
subtitle: Lead paint is thought to be a significant contributor to lead poisoning; many countries have therefore implemented a regulatory limit of 90 parts per million (ppm) or 600ppm per weight of dry paint.

title: Global phase-out of leaded petrol in road vehicles
subtitle: All countries have banned the use of leaded petrol in road vehicles. Algeria was the final country to do so in 2021.

title: Leading cancer types causing death in men
subtitle: The most common cause of cancer deaths in men, based on the underlying cause listed on death certificates.

title: Leading cancer types causing death in women
subtitle: The most common cause of cancer deaths in women, based on the underlying cause listed on death certificates.

title: Leading cause of child mortality among children under five
Leading causes of death
subtitle: The disease, condition, or injury estimated to cause the most deaths in each country annually.

title: Which countries have legally-binding controls on lead paint?
subtitle: Paint is a main contributor to harmful lead exposure. The stringency of controls on lead paint can vary by country. Maximum concentrations of lead can differ, and may only apply to particular types of paint (for example, products used in households).

title: Legal frameworks addressing gender equality in employment and economic benefits
subtitle: A higher percentage indicates stronger legislation.

title: Legal frameworks addressing gender equality within marriage and family
subtitle: A higher percentage indicates stronger legislation.

title: Legal frameworks addressing violence against women
subtitle: A higher percentage indicates stronger legislation.

title: Share of adults with legal documentation of their rights to land
subtitle: The proportion of the total adult population with secure tenure rights to land, recognized with legal documentation.

title: Legislation on domestic violence
subtitle: The law on domestic violence may punish offenders, provide protection orders for victims, or address harassment that causes physical or mental harm.

title: Legislative Corruption Score
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which members of the legislature abuse their position for financial gain, such as bribes, government contracts, future employment, or stealing from the state. Higher scores mean less corruption. A score of 0 is approximately the average across all countries and years.

title: Score of adoption and implementation of national strategies for managing disaster risk
subtitle: Score from 0 (worst) to 1 (best) measuring alignment of country disaster risk reduction strategies with the Sendai Framework.

title: Level of national compliance with labor rights
subtitle: The indicator has a range from 0 to 10, with 0 being the best possible score (indicating higher levels of compliance with fundamental rights at work) and 10 the worst (indicating lower levels of compliance with fundamental rights at work).

title: LGBT+ Legal Equality Index
subtitle: The index captures to which extent LGBT+ people have the same rights as straight and cisgender people. It combines 15 individual policies, such as the legality of same-sex relationships, marriage, and gender marker changes. It ranges from 0 to 100 (most equal).

title: LGBT+ Rights Index
subtitle: The index captures the extent to which LGBT+ people have the same rights as straight and cisgender people. It combines 35 policy measures, such as the legality of same-sex relationships, marriage, and gender marker changes. Higher values indicate more rights; negative values indicate that regressive policies dominate.

title: Liberal Democracy Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent of voting rights, the freedom and fairness of elections, freedoms of association and expression, civil liberties, and executive constraints. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most democratic).

title: Liberal Political Institutions Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent of individual and minority rights, equality before the law, and constraints on the executive by the legislature and courts. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most liberal).

title: Life expectancy
Life expectancy at age 15
subtitle: The period life expectancy for people who have reached the age of 15, in a given year. From 2022 onwards, the UN WPP's mid-variant projections are shown.

title: Life expectancy at birth
subtitle: The period life expectancy is the age to which a newborn can expect to live, if age-specific mortality rates in the current year were to stay the same throughout their life. Future projections are based on the UN's medium scenario.

title: Life expectancy
subtitle: The period life expectancy at birth, in a given year.

title: Life expectancy
subtitle: Average number of years a newborn would live if age-specific mortality rates in the current year were to stay the same throughout its life.

title: Life expectancy at birth
subtitle: The period life expectancy is the age to which a newborn can expect to live, if age-specific mortality rates in the current year were to stay the same throughout their life.

title: Share of women who are expected to die from pregnancy-related causes
subtitle: The probability that a 15 year old girl eventually dies from a pregnancy-related cause, assuming constant levels of maternal mortality and number of births per woman.

title: Data instruments used to estimate literacy
subtitle: This figure illustrates the type of sources that countries use to estimate literacy rates. The three categories include censuses (e.g. national population censuses), surveys (e.g. Demographic and Health Surveys), and indirect inference (e.g. extrapolation from educational attainment data).

title: Lithium production
subtitle: Lithium production is measured in tonnes.

title: Living languages
subtitle: A living language has at least one person speaking it as their first language.

title: Share of local governments that implemented local disaster risk reduction strategies in line with national strategies
Share of local governments with disaster risk reduction strategies
subtitle: Share of local governments that have adopted and implemented local disaster risk reduction strategies in line with the national strategy.

title: Countries where armed conflicts took place
subtitle: Included are armed conflicts that caused at least one death in the country that year.

title: Birth rate
subtitle: The total number of births per 1,000 people in a given year.

title: Childhood stunting rates
subtitle: Share of 2-to-10-year-olds who are defined as stunted. Stunting is when a child is significantly shorter than the average for their age. It is a consequence of poor nutrition or repeated infection.

title: Share of population living in urbanized areas
Lower secondary school completion rates, adjusted gender parity index
Farm machinery per unit of agricultural land
subtitle: Farm machinery is measured in units of horsepower. This is divided by total agricultural land to give the average machinery use per hectare of agricultural land.

title: Corn production
subtitle: Corn (maize) production is measured in tonnes.

title: Death rate from malaria
subtitle: Estimated number of deaths from malaria per 100,000 people.

title: Number of deaths from malaria
subtitle: Estimated number of deaths from malaria.

title: Male homicide rate
subtitle: Annual number of homicides where the victim was male, per 100,000 males.

title: Male labor force participation rate
subtitle: Share of the male working-age population (ages 15 and over) who are economically active (employed or unemployed).

title: Male-to-female height ratio by year of birth
subtitle: Ratio between the mean height of adult men and women, by birth year. Values greater than 1 indicate the mean height of men is greater than that of women.

title: Death rate from malnutrition
subtitle: Estimated death rate from protein-energy malnutrition per 100,000 people. Comparisons between countries and over time may be affected by differences in diagnostic practices and death certification.

title: Which countries have mandatory childhood vaccination policies?
subtitle: Countries are mapped based on having requirements or recommendations for at least one vaccine in 2019.

title: Manufacturing jobs as a share of total employment
Share of manufacturing in gross domestic product (GDP)
subtitle: Manufacturing comprises units engaged in the physical, or chemical transformation of materials, substances, or components into new products.

title: Countries with gender-equal inheritance
subtitle: Figure distinguishes between the countries that have gender-equal inheritance for women, and those which do not.

title: Share of marine territorial waters that are protected
subtitle: Marine protected areas are regions of intertidal or sub-tidal land and associated water, flora and fauna, and cultural and historical features that have been legally or effectively reserved for protection.

title: Marriage rates
Marriage for same-sex partners
Maternal mortality ratio
subtitle: Estimated number of women who die from maternal conditions per 100,000 live births, based on data from death certificates, large-scale surveys, and statistical modeling.

title: Maternal mortality ratio
subtitle: Estimated number of women who die from maternal conditions per 100,000 live births.

title: Maternal mortality ratio
subtitle: Estimated number of women who die from maternal conditions per 100,000 live births.

title: Mean body mass index (BMI) in men
subtitle: Body mass index (BMI) is measured as a person's weight in kilograms (kg) divided by his height (in meters), squared. The WHO define a BMI <=18.5 as 'underweight'; 18.5 to <25 as 'normal/healthy'; 25.0 to <30 as 'overweight'; and >30.0 as 'obese'.

title: Mean body mass index (BMI) in women
subtitle: Body mass index (BMI) is measured as a person's weight in kilograms (kg) divided by her height (in meters), squared. The WHO define a BMI <=18.5 as 'underweight'; 18.5 to <25 as 'normal/healthy'; 25.0 to <30 as 'overweight'; and >30.0 as 'obese'.

title: Average years of schooling
subtitle: Average years of formal education for individuals aged 15-64.

title: Meat production
subtitle: Expressed in tonnes. Includes cattle, poultry, sheep/mutton, goat, pigmeat, and wild game.

title: Meat supply per person
subtitle: Average total meat supply per person measured in kilograms per year.

title: Mechanisms in place to enhance policy coherence for sustainable development
subtitle: A composite indicator which covers mechanisms related to: 1) Institutionalisation of political commitment 2) Long-term considerations in decision-making 3) Inter-ministerial and cross-sectoral coordination 4) Participatory processes 5) Policy linkages 6) Alignment across government levels 7) Monitoring and reporting for policy coherence 8) Financing for policy coherence. Score expressed as a percentage of the maximum.

title: Median age
subtitle: The median age is the age that divides the population into two equal halves — half of the population is younger, and half is older. Future projections are based on the UN's medium scenario.

title: Median income per year (after tax)
subtitle: This data is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries. Income here is measured after taxes and benefits.

title: Level of implementation of sustainable procurement policies and  plans
subtitle: Evaluation of a country’s sustainable public procurement implementation level, scope, and comprehensiveness is scored based on six parameters. These parameters consider the existence of regulatory frameworks, implementation support, monitoring, and the share of products and services purchased sustainably.

title: Share of young men who experienced sexual violence as children
subtitle: Men aged 18-29 years old who experienced any form of sexual violence before reaching the age of 18.

title: Value of exported goods as  a share of GDP
subtitle: Total value of merchandise exports divided by gross domestic product (GDP), expressed as a percentage.

title: Value of imported goods as a share of GDP
subtitle: Total value of merchandise imports divided by gross domestic product (GDP), expressed as a percentage.

title: Value of imported goods as a share of GDP
subtitle: Estimates correspond to merchandise import-to-GDP ratios for countries and regions. All ratios are taken at current prices. See source for more details.

title: Methane emissions
subtitle: Methane (CH₄) emissions are measured in tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalents. Emissions from fossil fuels, industry, agriculture, and land-use change are included.

title: Migrant recruitment costs
subtitle: The amount that migrant workers pay to find, qualify for, secure and reach their first job abroad, divided by their average monthly salary. A higher value indicates a more costly location to migrate to for employment.

title: Share of the population born in another country
Total number of international immigrants
subtitle: An immigrant is someone who lives in a country that they were not born in.

title: Military spending as a share of government spending
subtitle: Military expenditure divided by government spending, expressed as a percentage. Includes military and civil personnel, operation and maintenance, procurement, military research and development, infrastructure, and aid.

title: Military personnel as a share of total population
subtitle: Share of the total population under the command of the national government, intended for use against foreign adversaries and held ready for combat as of 1 January of the given year.

title: Military spending as a share of GDP
subtitle: Military expenditure divided by gross domestic product, expressed as a percentage.

title: Military spending as a share of GDP
subtitle: Military expenditure divided by gross domestic product, expressed as a percentage. Includes military and civil personnel, operation and maintenance, procurement, military research and development, infrastructure, and aid.

title: Military spending per armed forces personnel
subtitle: Includes military and civil personnel, operation and maintenance, procurement, military research and development, infrastructure, and aid. This data is expressed in US dollars and adjusted for inflation.

title: Military spending
subtitle: Includes military and civil personnel, operation and maintenance, procurement, military research and development, infrastructure, and aid. This data is expressed in US dollars and adjusted for inflation.

title: Milk production
Milk per animal
Minimum daily requirement of calories
subtitle: The minimum amount of daily dietary energy per person that is considered adequate to ensure they maintain a minimum weight for health. Across a population, this takes factors such as the age, sex, height, and activity levels of different individuals into account.

title: Mismanaged plastic waste per capita
subtitle: Mismanaged plastic waste is waste that is not recycled, incinerated, or kept in sealed landfills. It includes materials burned in open pits, dumped into seas or open waters, or disposed of in unsanitary landfills and dumpsites.

title: Mobile phone subscriptions
Mobile phone subscriptions per 100 people
subtitle: This number can get over 100 when the average person has more than one subscription to a mobile service.

title: Methodologies used for measuring literacy
subtitle: The figure illustrates how literacy rates have been recorded by countries over time. Methodologies include self declarations by individuals or other household members, literacy tests, and indirect estimates (e.g. by assuming literacy from educational attainment).

title: Female employment rate
Money committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure
subtitle: Public-private partnerships are any contractual arrangement between a public entity or authority and a private entity, for providing a public asset or service, in which the private party bears significant risk and management responsibility.

title: Money sent or brought back by migrants as a share of GDP
subtitle: Money sent or brought back by migrants refers to remittances a country has received in this year.

title: Monthly temperature anomalies
Expected share of deaths from non-communicable diseases
subtitle: The estimated share of 30-year-olds who would die before their 70th birthday from common non-communicable diseases: any of cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, or chronic respiratory disease.

title: Death rate attributable to unsafe water, sanitation, and hygiene
subtitle: Death rate attributed to unsafe water, unsafe sanitation or lack of hygiene (WASH), measured as the number of deaths per 100,000 people of a given population.

title: What is the most common religious affiliation in each country?
subtitle: Religious affiliation with the highest population share in 2020.

title: Mountain Green Cover Index
subtitle: Mountain Green Cover Index measures the share of mountainous areas covered by either forest, cropland, grassland or wetland. An increase in green mountain cover may reflect either the expansion of natural ecosystems or an increase in the growth of vegetation in areas previously covered by glaciers.

title: Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)
subtitle: Multidimensional poverty is defined as being deprived in a range of health, education and living standards indicators. The MPI is a measure that combines the prevalence and the intensity of multidimensional poverty on a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate higher poverty.

title: Municipal waste recycled
subtitle: Waste from households that is collected by local authorities and recycled.

title: Municipal water as a share of total water withdrawals
subtitle: Municipal (domestic) water withdrawals as a percentage of total water withdrawals (which is the sum of water used for agriculture, industry, and municipal purposes).

title: Municipal water withdrawal
subtitle: Total water withdrawal for municipal (domestic) purposes, measured in cubic meters (m³) per year. Municipal water is the annual quantity of water withdrawn primarily for the direct use by the population.

title: National biodiversity strategy and action plan targets align with Aichi Biodiversity Target 9
subtitle: Aichi Target 9: By 2020, invasive alien species and pathways are identified and prioritized, priority species are controlled or eradicated and measures are in place to manage pathways to prevent their introduction and establishment.

title: National progress towards Aichi Biodiversity Target 2
subtitle: Aichi Target 2: By 2020, at the latest, biodiversity values have been integrated into national and local development and poverty reduction strategies and planning processes and are being incorporated into national accounting and reporting systems.

title: Existence of a national strategy for youth employment
Systems to monitor the spread of antimicrobial resistance in humans
subtitle: The type of system to monitor the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in common bacterial infections.

title: Number of deaths from natural disasters
subtitle: Annual number of deaths from all forms of natural disasters.

title: Natural population growth rate
subtitle: Annual population change determined by births and deaths. Migration is not included. In this future scenario, net migration is set to zero from 2024 onwards, while mortality and fertility assumptions follow the UN's medium scenario; this means feedback between migration and these factors are not incorporated.

title: Total natural resource rents
subtitle: Natural resources rents are estimated as the difference between the price of a commodity and the average cost of producing it. Total natural resources rents are the sum of oil rents, natural gas rents, coal rents, mineral rents, and forest rents.

title: Share who say they would not want neighbors of a different religion
subtitle: Share of survey respondents who selected "neighbors of a different religion" when they were asked: "On this list are various groups of people. Could you please mention any that you would not like to have as neighbors?"

title: Neonatal mortality rate
subtitle: Estimated share of newborns who die before 28 days of age. A rate of 1% means one death for every 100 live births.

title: Net official development assistance to medical research and basic health sectors
subtitle: Net official development assistance to medical research and basic health sectors. This data is expressed in US dollars. It is adjusted for inflation but does not account for differences in living costs between countries.

title: Status of net-zero carbon emissions targets
subtitle: The inclusion criteria for net-zero commitments may vary from country to country. For example, the inclusion of international aviation emissions; or the acceptance of carbon offsets. To see the year for which countries have pledged to achieve net-zero, hover over the country in the interactive version of this chart.

title: Number of new book titles published per million people
Number of new cases of HIV
New cases of malaria per 100 people
subtitle: Number of malaria infections each year, per 100 people within the population. In high-burden areas, some people often suffer from multiple infections a year, so this metric can be different from the share of the population infected.

title: New tetanus infection rate
subtitle: New infections of tetanus are measured per 100,000 people in a given population.

title: Annual new cases of neonatal tetanus per million people
Nitrogen use efficiency
subtitle: Nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) is the ratio between nitrogen inputs and output. A NUE of 40% means that only 40% of nitrogen inputs are converted into nitrogen in the form of crops.

title: Nitrous oxide emissions
subtitle: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions are measured in tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalents.

title: Non-fatal occupational injury rates
subtitle: The frequency of non-fatal occupational injuries, shown as the number of cases per 100,000 employees.

title: Northern white rhino population
subtitle: Estimated number of Northern White rhinos.

title: Number of agri-environmental policies in place
subtitle: Policies include those targetting the environmental impacts of agriculture, which include outcomes such as fertilizer and pesticide use, land use, biodiversity and forests.

title: Number of airline passengers per year
subtitle: This represents the total rather than unique passenger activity: this means a person who makes multiple trips is counted multiple times.

title: Number of people who cannot afford a calorie sufficient diet
subtitle: The cost of an energy sufficient diet is the cheapest way that an individual can meet their calorie requirement using available staple foods in each country. A diet is defined as unaffordable when its cost, plus basic non-food needs like housing and transportation, exceeds daily income.

title: Child deaths linked to child and maternal malnutrition
subtitle: The number of under-five deaths which are attributed to child or maternal malnutrition as a risk factor.

title: Malnutrition: Number of children who are stunted
subtitle: The number of children younger than five who are stunted – significantly shorter than the average for their age, as a consequence of poor nutrition or repeated infection.

title: Number of unique plant genetic samples in conservation facilities
subtitle: The conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture (GRFA) in medium-long term conservation facilities represents the most trusted means of conserving plant genetic resources worldwide.

title: Number of Asian elephants
subtitle: Estimates on wild mammal populations tend to come with significant uncertainty.

title: Number of births
subtitle: Future projections are based on the UN's medium scenario.

title: Number of child deaths
subtitle: The number of children dying before reaching the age of five.

title: Number of child deaths
subtitle: Estimated number of children under the age of five who die each year.

title: Annual number of children newly infected with HIV
subtitle: Annual number of new cases of HIV in children aged 0-14 years old.

title: Children orphaned due to AIDS deaths
subtitle: Number of children, aged 17 and under, who have been orphaned by the death of one or both parents from HIV/AIDS at any point in their lives.

title: Number of clinical trials
subtitle: Annual number of completed clinical trials registered in the ClinicalTrials.gov database for each country. Registration in the ClinicalTrials database in the is mandatory for trials in the United States, but voluntary for other countries.

title: Commercial bank branches
subtitle: Number of commercial bank branches per 100,000 adults. Commercial bank branches are retail locations of resident commercial banks and other resident banks that function as commercial banks to provide financial services to customers.

title: Total COVID-19 tests per confirmed case
subtitle: Comparisons across countries are affected by differences in testing policies and reporting methods.

title: Number of deaths from pneumonia in children under five
subtitle: Death estimates also include deaths from other lower respiratory tract infections, of which clinically diagnosed pneumonia is the leading cause.

title: Deaths from road injuries
subtitle: Annual number of deaths from road injuries. Road injuries include deaths of drivers, passengers, pedestrians and cyclists.

title: Number of suicides
subtitle: Estimated annual number of deaths from suicide. Suicide deaths are underreported in many countries due to social stigma and cultural or legal concerns. This data includes modeling based on global suicide patterns, and includes adjustments and extrapolations that aim to account for missing data and underreporting.

title: Number of deaths from tetanus
subtitle: The estimated annual number of deaths from tetanus.

title: Number of deaths from tobacco smoking
subtitle: Estimated annual number of deaths attributed to smoking.

title: Number of deaths
subtitle: Future projections are based on the UN's medium scenario.

title: Paralytic polio: estimated cases by world region
subtitle: Estimates of the total number of paralytic polio cases, due to wild poliovirus and vaccine-derived polioviruses.

title: Employment in tourism-related industries per 1,000 people
Number of people using the Internet
subtitle: Number of people who used the Internet in the last three months.

title: Number of maternal deaths
subtitle: Estimated annual number of women who die from maternal conditions.

title: Number of neonatal deaths
subtitle: The estimated number of neonates – babies under 28 days old – who die each year.

title: Number of neonatal deaths
subtitle: The estimated number of neonates – newborns under 28 days of age – who die each year.

title: New HIV infections averted by prevention of mother-to-child transmission
subtitle: Prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) is a range of services provided to mothers at risk of HIV infection. Data is shown for children younger than 14 years.

title: Number of people employed in agriculture
subtitle: Agriculture includes the cultivation of crops and livestock production, as well as forestry, hunting, and fishing. Employment includes anyone engaged in any activity to produce goods or services for pay or profit.

title: Number of people living in the capital city
subtitle: City boundaries are defined using a consistent global approach based on satellite imagery and population data.

title: Number of people living with HIV
subtitle: The estimated number of current cases of HIV/AIDS.

title: Refugees by country of origin per 100,000 people
Cholera reported deaths
Reported cases of guinea worm disease
subtitle: Reported annual cases of guinea worm disease. Guinea worm disease is a painful and debilitating disease caused by a parasitic worm spread through contaminated water.

title: Number of reported smallpox cases
subtitle: The reported number of smallpox cases each year. The historical number of smallpox cases reported is lower than the actual number of cases in those years, due to limited testing and reporting.

title: Number of rhinos poached
subtitle: Estimates of wild rhino poaching are recorded and reported by only a select number of countries. Data is based primarily on recorded poaching and fatalities by national authorities in national parks and reserves.

title: Transboundary animal breeds with conserved genetic material
subtitle: The number of animal breeds existing in more than one country, of which enough genetic material (e.g. semen, ova, embryos or tissue) is stored in genebank collections to reconstitute the breed in case of extinction.

title: Tuberculosis cases
subtitle: The estimated number of new and relapse tuberculosis cases arising in a given year. All forms of the disease are included, including cases in people living with HIV.

title: Number of youth deaths
subtitle: The estimated number of children under the age of 15 who die each year.

title: Number of people who are undernourished
subtitle: Undernourishment is measured as having a caloric intake that is insufficient to meet the minimum energy requirements necessary for a given individual.

title: People not using improved sanitation facilities
subtitle: Improved sanitation facilities are those designed to hygienically separate excreta from human contact. If no improved sanitation facility is available, people might practice open defecation or use unimproved sanitation facilities.

title: People without basic handwashing facilities
subtitle: Number of people without access to basic handwashing facilities, with soap and water.

title: Number of people without access to clean fuels for cooking
subtitle: Clean cooking fuels and technologies represent non-solid fuels such as natural gas, ethanol or electric technologies.

title: People not using improved drinking water sources
subtitle: Improved drinking water sources are designed to deliver safe water and include: piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected springs or wells, rainwater, and packaged or delivered water. If no safe and reliable water source is available, people use surface water sources or unprotected springs or wells.

title: People not using safely managed drinking water sources
subtitle: Safely managed drinking water facilities are improved drinking water sources that are located on premises, available when needed, and free from microbiological and priority chemical contamination.

title: Numeracy rate in men
subtitle: Share of men aged 16-65 years who can apply multiple steps involving calculation with common decimals, percentages, and fractions; simple measurement and spatial representation; and interpretation of relatively simple data and statistics in texts, tables, and graphs.

title: Numeracy rate in women
subtitle: Share of women aged 16-65 years who can apply multiple steps involving calculation with common decimals, percentages, and fractions; simple measurement and spatial representation; and interpretation of relatively simple data and statistics in texts, tables, and graphs.

title: Nurses and midwives per 1,000 people
Prevalence rate of obesity in adults
subtitle: Estimated prevalence of obesity in adults, based on general population surveys and statistical modeling. Obesity is a risk factor for chronic complications, including cardiovascular disease, and premature death.

title: Ocean science and research funding
subtitle: The share of gross domestic expenditure on research and development allocated to marine science and research.

title: Gross overseas development assistance from all donors for scholarships
subtitle: Scholarships are financial aid awards for individuals towards full-time studies or training courses in institutions of higher education in the donor country. This data is expressed in US dollars. It is adjusted for inflation but does not account for differences in living costs between countries.

title: Spending on government outsourcing as share of GDP
subtitle: Government outsourcing is used to buy goods and services from entities outside the government. It includes goods and services used by governments (e.g. accounting or IT services) and outsourced goods and services financed by government (e.g. medical treatments).

title: Oil rents as a share of GDP
subtitle: Economic profits generated from oil extraction, measured as the difference between production value and costs, expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product.

title: Percentage of one-person households
subtitle: Number of one-person households as a share of the total number of households. Estimates combine multiple sources, including cross-country surveys and census data.

title: Exposure to outdoor air pollution
subtitle: Annual population-weighted average concentration of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in the air, measured in micrograms per cubic meter (µg/m³). Exposure to fine particulate matter can pose significant health risks. This data includes pollution from human and natural sources.

title: Outdoor air pollution death rate
subtitle: Estimated number of deaths attributed to outdoor particulate matter pollution per 100,000 people.

title: Legal frameworks addressing gender equality overall
subtitle: A higher percentage indicates stronger legislation.

title: Palm oil imports
Oil palm production
subtitle: Oil palm production is measured in tonnes.

title: Oil palm fruit yields
subtitle: Yields are measured in tonnes per hectare.

title: Parkinson's disease prevalence
subtitle: Estimated number of people with Parkinson's disease per 100,000 people.

title: Participation rate in formal and non-formal education and training
subtitle: Share of youth and adults aged 15-64, who participated in formal and non-formal education and training in the last 12 months. Non-formal education can take place both within and outside educational institutions.

title: Annual patent applications per million people
Peak birth month
subtitle: For each year, the month with the highest average birth rate per day (1 = January, 12 = December).

title: Number of people who completed the initial COVID-19 vaccination protocol
subtitle: Total number of people who received all doses prescribed by the initial vaccination protocol.

title: Share of people practicing open defecation
subtitle: Open defecation refers to defecation in fields, forests, bushes, bodies of water, or other open spaces. This indicates a lack of safe sanitation infrastructure and poses risks, such as drinking water contamination and the spread of diseases.

title: Total number of people who received at least one dose of COVID-19 vaccine
Number of people without access to electricity
subtitle: Having access to electricity is defined in international statistics as having an electricity source that can provide very basic lighting, and charge a phone or power a radio for 4 hours per day.

title: Alcohol consumption per capita
subtitle: Average per capita alcohol consumption measured in litres of pure alcohol per person per year.

title: Per capita CO₂ emissions from aviation
subtitle: Aviation emissions include both domestic and international flights. International aviation emissions are allocated to the country of departure of each flight.

title: Per capita CO₂ emissions from cement
Per capita CO₂ emissions from coal
Per capita  CO₂ emissions from domestic commercial passenger flights
subtitle: Domestic aviation represents flights which depart and arrive within the same country.

title: Per capita CO₂ emissions from flaring
Per capita CO₂ emissions from deforestation for food production
subtitle: Tonnes of CO₂ emissions per person linked to deforestation for food production – it is trade-adjusted, to reflect the carbon footprint of diets within a given country. Based on the annual average over the period from 2010 to 2014.

title: Per capita CO₂ emissions from gas
Per capita CO₂ emissions from international aviation
subtitle: International aviation emissions are here allocated to the country of departure of each flight.

title: Per capita CO₂ emissions from international passenger flights, tourism-adjusted
subtitle: International aviation emissions are allocated to the country of departure, then adjusted for tourism.

title: Per capita CO₂ emissions from oil
Per capita CO₂ emissions from transport
subtitle: Measured in kilograms per person. International aviation and shipping emissions are not included.

title: Per capita egg consumption
subtitle: Average per capita egg consumption, measured in kilograms per year (in shell weight).

title: Per capita greenhouse gas emissions
subtitle: Greenhouse gas emissions include carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide from all sources, including land-use change. They are measured in tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalents over a 100-year timescale.

title: Per capita methane emissions
subtitle: Per capita methane emissions are measured in tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalents per person per year.

title: Milk  supply per person
subtitle: Average per capita milk supply, measured in kilograms per person per year. This includes the milk equivalents of dairy products made from milk ingredients, but excludes butter.

title: Per capita nitrous oxide emissions
subtitle: Per capita nitrous oxide emissions are measured in tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalents per person per year.

title: Plastic waste emitted to the ocean per capita
subtitle: This is an annual estimate of plastic emissions. A country's total does not include waste that is exported overseas, which may be at higher risk of entering the ocean.

title: Renewable freshwater resources per person
subtitle: Renewable internal freshwater resources refers to the quantity of internal freshwater from inflowing river basins and recharging groundwater aquifers. This is measured in cubic meters per person per year.

title: Year-to-year percentage change in primary energy use by source
subtitle: Change in total energy supply from the previous year, as a percentage.

title: Percentage of territory effectively controlled by government
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which the government is recognized as the main authority, or rejected by others, such as insurgent groups, criminal organizations, or other countries.

title: Share of women who report having been victims of forced sex as children
subtitle: Women aged 18 to 29 who report having experienced forced sex before the age of 18. Estimates come from surveys in the period 2005–2016.

title: Change in the share of the population that is religious between 2010 and 2020
subtitle: The percentage point change in the share that is affiliated with any religion. This is based on how people describe their own religious identity. Countries in red have seen a decline in religious affiliation; those in blue, an increase.

title: Average age of mothers at childbirth
subtitle: Estimated average age of women who have given birth in each year. This includes all births that year, not just women's first childbirth.

title: Pesticide use per hectare of cropland
subtitle: Average pesticide application per unit of cropland, measured in kilograms per hectare.

title: Pesticide use
subtitle: Total pesticide use measured in tonnes of pesticide consumption per year.

title: Pharmacists per 10,000 population
Physical Integrity Rights Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which people are free from government torture and political killings. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most rights).

title: Physical Integrity Rights Score
subtitle: The score captures the extent to which citizens are protected from government killings, torture, political imprisonments, extrajudicial executions, mass killings and disappearances. Large positive scores mean abuses are rare relative to other countries and years, large negative scores that abuses are relatively widespread.

title: Medical doctors per 1,000 people
Number of pigs
Pig meat per animal
subtitle: Pigmeat yields, measured in kilograms produced per animal.

title: Pig meat production
subtitle: Expressed in tonnes.

title: Plastic waste generation
subtitle: This measures total plastic waste generation prior to management and therefore does not represent the quantity of plastic at risk of polluting waterways, rivers and the ocean environment.

title: Mismanaged plastic waste
subtitle: Mismanaged plastic waste is waste that is not recycled, incinerated, or kept in sealed landfills. It includes materials burned in open pits, dumped into seas or open waters, or disposed of in unsanitary landfills and dumpsites.

title: Plastic waste generation per capita
subtitle: Daily plastic waste generation per person, measured in kilograms per person per day. This measures the overall per capita plastic waste generation rate prior to waste management, recycling or incineration. It does not therefore directly indicate the risk of pollution to waterways or marine environments.

title: Which countries include pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) in their national vaccination programs?
subtitle: This shows which countries provide and recommend pneumococcal conjugate vaccines through routine services. People may still be able to receive the vaccine if it's not in the routine schedule – it might be optional or available commercially.

title: Share of children with symptoms of pneumonia who are taken to a health provider
subtitle: The estimated share of children under five years old showing symptoms of pneumonia who are taken to a health provider.

title: Death rate from pneumonia
subtitle: The estimated annual death rate from pneumonia and other lower respiratory tract infections per 100,000 people.

title: Death rate from pneumonia and other lower respiratory infections in children
subtitle: The estimated annual death rate from pneumonia and other lower respiratory infections in children under five, per 100,000.

title: Police officers per 1,000 people
Where are we falling behind on screening and testing for polio?
subtitle: Countries are considered to have adequate screening if they have a non-polio acute flaccid paralysis rate above 2 per 100,000 children, and adequate testing if they have a stool collection rate above 80%.

title: Share of one-year-olds who are vaccinated against polio
subtitle: Share of one-year-olds who have received the third dose of polio-containing vaccine. This may be either the oral or the inactivated polio vaccine.

title: Polio vaccine schedule
subtitle: The type of polio vaccines used in the national immunization schedule in each country: only inactivated poliovirus vaccines (IPV), oral poliovirus vaccines (OPV), or both.

title: Centralization of Political Power Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which the executive is unconstrained by the legislature, judiciary, electoral management body, and other oversight bodies. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most centralized).

title: Political Civil Liberties Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which people enjoy freedom of expression and association. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (most liberties).

title: Political Corruption Index
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which the executive, legislative, judiciary, and bureaucracy engage in bribery and theft, and the making and implementation of laws are susceptible to corruption. The index ranges from 0 to 1 (highly corrupt).

title: Political Polarization Score
subtitle: Data by V-Dem. Expert estimates of the extent to which society is divided into hostile political camps, and political differences undermine social relationships and discourage interaction across ideological lines. Higher scores indicate more polarization. A score of 0 is approximately the average across all countries and years.

title: Democracy
subtitle: Classification by Lührmann et al. (2018) based on expert estimates by V-Dem.

title: Democracy
subtitle: Data by the Economist Intelligence Unit.

title: Democratic change
subtitle: Data by Episodes of Regime Transformation and V-Dem.

title: Democracy
subtitle: Data by Episodes of Regime Transformation and V-Dem.

title: Democracy
subtitle: Data by the Lexical Index of Electoral Democracy.

title: Air pollution deaths from fossil fuels
subtitle: This measures annual excess mortality from the health impacts of air pollution from fossil fuels.

title: Population
Population census recently completed
subtitle: Population census completed in the last 10 years. Population censuses collect data on the size, distribution and composition of the population.

title: Population census recently completed
subtitle: Population census completed in the last 10 years. Population censuses collect data on the size, distribution and composition of the population.

title: Population density
subtitle: Number of people per km² of land area.

title: Population growth rate
subtitle: Annual population change determined by births, deaths, and migration, expressed as a percentage of the population. Future projections are based on the UN's medium scenario.

title: Share of urban population who live in the largest city
subtitle: Estimated share of urban population (the sum of cities and towns and suburbs) living in the largest city. City boundaries are defined using a consistent global approach based on satellite imagery and population data.

title: Population
subtitle: Future projections are based on the UN's medium-fertility scenario.

title: Has the population peaked?
subtitle: Whether the population has passed its highest value between 1950 and 2100, based on UN estimates and medium-scenario projections.

title: Country has a population register
subtitle: Population registers are centralized state agencies that keep detailed and permanently updated records of every person in the territory.

title: Population
Share of population using at least a basic drinking water source
subtitle: A basic drinking water service is water from an improved water source that can be collected within a 30-minute round trip, including queuing.

title: Share of population with alcohol use disorders
subtitle: The percentage of people aged over 15 who have had an alcohol use disorder within the last year.

title: Population
subtitle: Future projections are based on the UN's medium scenario.

title: The share of COVID-19 tests that are positive
subtitle: DEPRECATED CHART. 7-day rolling average. Comparisons across countries are affected by differences in testing policies and reporting methods.

title: Potato production
subtitle: Potato production is measured in tonnes.

title: Number of poultry birds
Poultry production
subtitle: Expressed in tonnes.

title: Poultry meat per animal
Poverty gap index at $3 a day
subtitle: The poverty gap index is a poverty measure that reflects both the prevalence and the depth of poverty. It is calculated as the share of population in poverty multiplied by the average shortfall from the poverty line (expressed as a % of the poverty line).

title: Power outages in firms in a typical month
subtitle: Power outages are the average number of power outages that firms experience in a typical month.

title: PPP conversion factor for private consumption
Number of people with cysticercosis per 100,000
subtitle: Estimated number people with cysticercosis per 100,000 people in the population. Cysticercosis is a parasitic tissue infection of tissues (including brain and muscle tissue) caused by larval cysts of a tapeworm that can cause seizures.

title: Share of children who have anemia
subtitle: Share of children under the age of five with anemia. Anemia is a condition that develops when your blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin.

title: Share of pregnant women who have anemia
subtitle: Anemia is a condition that develops when your blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin.

title: Share of women of reproductive age who have anemia
subtitle: Share of women of reproductive age (aged 15-49) with anemia. Anemia is a condition that develops when your blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin.

title: Share of children with an active hepatitis B infection
subtitle: The share of five year old children who test positive for a marker of infection called hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). A positive test for HBsAg indicates an active hepatitis B virus infection.

title: Number of people with lymphatic filariasis
subtitle: The estimated number of people living with lymphatic filariasis. Lymphatic filariasis is a highly debilitating parasitic disease caused by microscopic worms.

title: Share of children under five who have night blindness
